view(CaseStudy1.data)
Frito_base <- CaseStudy1.data

summary(Frito_base)

#Change data types
Frito_base <- Frito_base %>%
  mutate(
    Age = as.numeric(Age),
    Attrition = as.factor(Attrition),
    BusinessTravel = as.factor(BusinessTravel),
    DailyRate = as.numeric(DailyRate),
    DistanceFromHome = as.numeric(DistanceFromHome),
    Education = as.factor(Education),
    EducationField = as.factor(EducationField),
    EnvironmentSatisfaction = as.factor(EnvironmentSatisfaction),
    Gender = as.factor(Gender),
    HourlyRate = as.numeric(HourlyRate),
    JobInvolvement = as.factor(JobInvolvement),
    JobLevel = as.factor(JobLevel),
    JobRole = as.factor(JobRole),
    JobSatisfaction = as.factor(JobSatisfaction),
    MaritalStatus = as.factor(MaritalStatus),
    MonthlyIncome = as.numeric(MonthlyIncome),
    MonthlyRate = as.numeric(MonthlyRate),
    NumCompaniesWorked = as.numeric(NumCompaniesWorked),
    Over18 = as.factor(Over18),
    OverTime = as.factor(OverTime),
    PercentSalaryHike = as.numeric(PercentSalaryHike),
    PerformanceRating = as.factor(PerformanceRating),
    RelationshipSatisfaction = as.factor(RelationshipSatisfaction),
    StandardHours = as.numeric(StandardHours),
    StockOptionLevel = as.factor(StockOptionLevel),
    TotalWorkingYears = as.numeric(TotalWorkingYears),
    TrainingTimesLastYear = as.numeric(TrainingTimesLastYear),
    WorkLifeBalance = as.factor(WorkLifeBalance),
    YearsAtCompany = as.numeric(YearsAtCompany),
    YearsInCurrentRole = as.numeric(YearsInCurrentRole),
    YearsSinceLastPromotion = as.numeric(YearsSinceLastPromotion),
    YearsWithCurrManager = as.numeric(YearsWithCurrManager)
  )
view(Frito_base)

#Develop Attrition into numeric binary
Frito_base$Attrition_Num <- ifelse(Frito_base$Attrition == "Yes",1,0)


#Creating variable groups rather than just numeric values
age_breaks <- c(0,25,30,40,50,100)
age_labels <- c("Under 25","26-29","30-39","40-49","50+")
Frito_base$Age_Groups <- cut(
  Frito_base$Age, 
  breaks = age_breaks,
  labels = age_labels,
  right = FALSE
)

Income_breaks <- c(0,2500,5000,7500,10000,12500,15000,17500,20000)
Income_labels <- c("Under $2,500","$2,500-$4,999","$5,000-$7,499","$7,500-<$9,999","$10,000-$12,499","$12,500-$14,999","$15,000-$17,499","$17,500+")
Frito_base$Income_Groups <- cut(
  Frito_base$MonthlyIncome, 
  breaks = Income_breaks,
  labels = Income_labels,
  right = FALSE
)

HrRate_breaks <- c(0,40,60,80,100)
HrRate_labels <- c("Under $40","$40-$59","$60-$79","$80+")
Frito_base$HrRate_Groups <- cut(
  Frito_base$HourlyRate, 
  breaks = HrRate_breaks,
  labels = HrRate_labels,
  right = FALSE
)

DailyRate_breaks <- c(0,300,500,700,900,1100,1300,1500)
DailyRate_labels <- c("Under $300","$300-$500","$500-$700","$700-$900","$900-$1,100","$1,100-$1,300","$1,300+")
Frito_base$DailyRate_Groups <- cut(
  Frito_base$DailyRate, 
  breaks = DailyRate_breaks,
  labels = DailyRate_labels,
  right = FALSE
)

MonthlyRate_breaks <- c(0,6000,10000,14000,18000,22000,28000)
MonthlyRate_labels <- c("Under $6000","$6000-$10000","$10000-$14000","$14000-$18000","$18000-$22000","$22000+")
Frito_base$MonthlyRate_Groups <- cut(
  Frito_base$MonthlyRate, 
  breaks = MonthlyRate_breaks,
  labels = MonthlyRate_labels,
  right = FALSE
)

Dist_breaks <- c(0,10,20,30)
Dist_labels <- c("Close","Mid","Far")
Frito_base$Dist_Group <- cut(
  Frito_base$DistanceFromHome, 
  breaks = Dist_breaks,
  labels = Dist_labels,
  right = FALSE
)

Compyears_breaks <- c(0,5,10,15,20,25,30)
Compyears_labels <- c("<5","5-10","10-15","15-20","20-25","25-30")
Frito_base$CompYears_Group <- cut(
  Frito_base$YearsAtCompany, 
  breaks = Compyears_breaks,
  labels = Compyears_labels,
  right = FALSE
)

Posyears_breaks <- c(0,3,6,9,12,30)
Posyears_labels <- c("<3","3-6","6-9","9-12","12+")
Frito_base$PosYears_Group <- cut(
  Frito_base$YearsInCurrentRole, 
  breaks = Posyears_breaks,
  labels = Posyears_labels,
  right = FALSE
)

#Group used to evaluate attriton costs according to article offered
Frito_base <- Frito_base %>%
  mutate(JobLevelName = case_when(
    as.numeric(as.character(JobLevel)) %in% c(1, 2) ~ "Entry",
    as.numeric(as.character(JobLevel)) == 3         ~ "Mid-Tier",
    as.numeric(as.character(JobLevel)) %in% c(4, 5) ~ "Senior",
    TRUE                                           ~ NA_character_
  ))

#Probability of costs used to evaluate attrition costs according to article offered
Frito_base <- Frito_base %>%
  mutate(Attrition_Cost_Ratio = case_when(
    as.numeric(as.character(JobLevel)) %in% c(1, 2) ~ ".4",
    as.numeric(as.character(JobLevel)) == 3         ~ "1.35",
    as.numeric(as.character(JobLevel)) %in% c(4, 5) ~ "4",
    TRUE                                           ~ NA_character_
  ))
Frito_base <- Frito_base %>% mutate(Attrition_Cost_Ratio=as.numeric(Attrition_Cost_Ratio))

Frito_base$Attrition_Monthly_Cost = Frito_base$Attrition_Cost_Ratio*Frito_base$MonthlyIncome

Frito_base %>%
  group_by(JobLevelName) %>%
  summarise(mean_value = mean(Attrition_Monthly_Cost, na.rm = TRUE))

###Re-ordering data for more logical basis if reviewing data in excel
Frito_base <- Frito_base %>%

         "MonthlyRate_Groups", "MonthlyIncome","Income_Groups","PercentSalaryHike","Age","Age_Groups","Gender",
          "MaritalStatus","Education","EducationField","DistanceFromHome","Dist_Group","OverTime",
          "Department","JobRole","JobLevel","JobLevelName","JobInvolvement","JobSatisfaction","EnvironmentSatisfaction",
          "RelationshipSatisfaction","PerformanceRating","WorkLifeBalance","StockOptionLevel","BusinessTravel",
          "YearsInCurrentRole","PosYears_Group","YearsAtCompany","CompYears_Group","NumCompaniesWorked",
          "TrainingTimesLastYear","YearsSinceLastPromotion","TotalWorkingYears","YearsWithCurrManager",
          "StandardHours","EmployeeCount","Over18","EmployeeNumber","ID")

##################################################################################
                  ####  KNN on only Key Attributes to Attrition   ####
                     ######## Varied Threshold Included  ########
##################################################################################

# Attrition Cost varied by Employee Type, See "Attrition_Monthly_Cost" and Attrition prob table by JobLevelName
# Avg Attrition Cost = Job level * Cost * 6-9 months --> 
#     18.1%*$1643 (Entry) + 12.9%*13300 (Mid) + 7.2%*$67072 (Senior) = $6831/month * 6 months = $40,986/employee
AttritionCost = 40986
AttritionIncentive = 200
threshold = .4      ### Standard is .5

KNN_frito <- Frito_base[,c("JobLevel","JobInvolvement",
                           "Age", "MonthlyIncome","YearsAtCompany","YearsInCurrentRole","YearsWithCurrManager",
                           "Attrition")]

KNN_frito_clean <- na.omit(KNN_frito)
KNN_frito_clean[,1] <- as.numeric(as.factor(KNN_frito_clean[,1]))
KNN_frito_clean[,2] <- as.numeric(as.factor(KNN_frito_clean[,2]))

view(KNN_frito_clean)

classifications = knn(
  train = KNN_frito_clean[,1:7],
  test = KNN_frito_clean[,1:7],
  cl = KNN_frito_clean[,8],
  prob = TRUE,
  k = 10
)
table(classifications,KNN_frito_clean[,8],dnn = c("Prediction","Actual"))

CM_KNN = confusionMatrix(table(classifications,KNN_frito_clean[,8]), mode = "everything")
CM_KNN

#Add Costs
KNN_Cost_Est = AttritionCost*(CM_KNN$table[3]+CM_KNN$table[4]) + AttritionIncentive*(CM_KNN$table[2])
KNN_Cost_Attr = AttritionCost*(CM_KNN$table[3]+CM_KNN$table[4])
KNN_Cost_inc = AttritionIncentive*(CM_KNN$table[2])
KNN_Cost_Est #Actual Attrition Cost for everyone that leaves + $200 per false predict attrition
KNN_Cost_Attr
KNN_Cost_inc

##################################################################################
           # Naive Bayes Modelling w/ Varied Thresholds ######
##################################################################################

### Correlating Factors at 50% ###
#set.seed(1)
train_index  <- sample(1:dim(Frito_base)[1], round(.7 * dim(Frito_base)[1]))
train_data   <- Frito_base[train_index, ]
test_data    <- Frito_base[-train_index, ]

nb_model_1   <- naiveBayes(Attrition ~ Age_Groups + Income_Groups + JobInvolvement + 
                             JobLevel + JobRole + YearsAtCompany + YearsInCurrentRole + 
                             YearsWithCurrManager, data = train_data)
pred_probs   <- predict(nb_model_1, newdata = test_data, type = "raw")
pred_classes <- predict(nb_model_1, newdata = test_data, type = "class")
conf_matrix_1 <- confusionMatrix(data = pred_classes, reference = test_data$Attrition, dnn = c("Prediction", "Actual"))
print(nb_model_1)
print(conf_matrix_1)

### 2. Multi-Iteration Loop with Custom Threshold (0.4) ###
iterations <- 100  # Define how many times you want to split and test
# Pre-allocate numeric vectors to store metrics
masterAcc  <- numeric(iterations)
masterSens <- numeric(iterations)
masterSpec <- numeric(iterations)
for (j in 1:iterations) {
  # New random split per iteration
  train_index <- sample(1:dim(Frito_base)[1], round(.7 * dim(Frito_base)[1]))
  train_data  <- Frito_base[train_index, ]
  test_data   <- Frito_base[-train_index, ]
  # Train model
  nb_model_loop <- naiveBayes(Attrition ~ Age_Groups + Income_Groups + JobInvolvement + 
                                JobLevel + JobRole + YearsAtCompany + YearsInCurrentRole + 
                                YearsWithCurrManager, data = train_data)
  # Predict probabilities on the loop's test data
  pred_probs <- predict(nb_model_loop, newdata = test_data, type = "raw")
  # Apply the custom 0.4 threshold for "Yes"
  threshold    <- 0.4
  pred_classes <- factor(ifelse(pred_probs[, "Yes"] > threshold, "Yes", "No"), 
                         levels = levels(test_data$Attrition))
  # Calculate confusion matrix metrics
  CM_1 <- confusionMatrix(data = pred_classes, reference = test_data$Attrition)
  # Save metrics into vectors
  masterAcc[j]  <- CM_1$overall["Accuracy"]
  masterSens[j] <- CM_1$byClass["Sensitivity"]
  masterSpec[j] <- CM_1$byClass["Specificity"]
}
# Calculate and display the final average performance
MeanAcc  <- mean(masterAcc)
MeanSens <- mean(masterSens)
MeanSpec <- mean(masterSpec)
MeanAcc
MeanSens
MeanSpec

### Kitchen Sink - Includes all provided data, including groupings constructed ###
#set.seed(1)
train_index <- sample(1:dim(Frito_base)[1],round(.7*dim(Frito_base)[1]))
train_data <- Frito_base[train_index,]
test_data <- Frito_base[-train_index,]
nb_model_ks <- naiveBayes(
  Attrition ~ HourlyRate+HrRate_Groups+DailyRate+MonthlyRate+MonthlyIncome+Income_Groups+PercentSalaryHike+
    Age+Age_Groups+Gender+MaritalStatus+Education+EducationField+DistanceFromHome+Dist_Group+OverTime+Department+
    JobRole+JobLevel+JobInvolvement+JobSatisfaction+EnvironmentSatisfaction+RelationshipSatisfaction+PerformanceRating+
    WorkLifeBalance+StockOptionLevel+BusinessTravel+YearsInCurrentRole+PosYears_Group+YearsAtCompany+CompYears_Group+
    NumCompaniesWorked+TrainingTimesLastYear+YearsSinceLastPromotion+TotalWorkingYears+YearsWithCurrManager, data = train_data)
pred_probs <- predict(nb_model_ks, newdata = test_data,type="raw")
pred_classes <- predict(nb_model_ks, newdata = test_data, type = "class")
conf_matrix_ks <- confusionMatrix(data = pred_classes, 
                                 reference = test_data$Attrition,
                                 dnn = c("Prediction","Actual"))
print(nb_model_ks)
print(conf_matrix_ks)

### Monte Carlo Simulation with Update Threshold Option###
set.seed(99)
iterations = 1000
masterAcc = matrix(nrow = iterations)
masterSens = matrix(nrow = iterations)
masterSpec = matrix(nrow = iterations)
splitPerc = .7 #Training / Test split Percentage
for(j in 1:iterations)
{
  trainIndices = sample(1:dim(Frito_base)[1],round(.7*dim(Frito_base)[1]))
  trainks100 = Frito_base[trainIndices,]
  testks100 = Frito_base[-trainIndices,]
  nb_model_ks1000 <- naiveBayes(
    Attrition ~ HourlyRate+HrRate_Groups+DailyRate+MonthlyRate+MonthlyIncome+Income_Groups+PercentSalaryHike+
      Age+Age_Groups+Gender+MaritalStatus+Education+EducationField+DistanceFromHome+Dist_Group+OverTime+Department+
      JobRole+JobLevel+JobInvolvement+JobSatisfaction+EnvironmentSatisfaction+RelationshipSatisfaction+PerformanceRating+
      WorkLifeBalance+StockOptionLevel+BusinessTravel+YearsInCurrentRole+PosYears_Group+YearsAtCompany+CompYears_Group+
      NumCompaniesWorked+TrainingTimesLastYear+YearsSinceLastPromotion+TotalWorkingYears+YearsWithCurrManager, 
    data = trainks1000
  )
pred_probs = predict(nb_model_ks1000, newdata = testks1000, type = "raw")
threshold = .4
pred_classes = factor(ifelse(pred_probs[,"Yes"] > threshold, "Yes","No"),
                      levels = levels(testks100$Attrition))
CM_ks1000 = confusionMatrix(data = pred_classes, reference = testks1000$Attrition)
masterAcc[j] = CM_ks1000$overall["Accuracy"]
masterSens[j] = CM_ks1000$byClass["Sensitivity"]
masterSpec[j] = CM_ks1000$byClass["Specificity"]
}
MeanAcc = colMeans(masterAcc)
MeanSens = colMeans(masterSens)
MeanSpec = colMeans(masterSpec)
MeanAcc
MeanSens
MeanSpec

CM_ks1000                       ### Best results between 100%-0%: 40% combined 78.5% acc, 81% sens, 64% spec ###

############    Company Attrition Characteristics Table - Formatted for PowerPoint ##############
Age_attrition <- Frito_base %>%
  group_by(Age_Groups) %>%
    summarise(
    total_employees = n(),
    Ex_employees = sum(Attrition == "Yes"),
    Attrition_perc = (Ex_employees / total_employees)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Attrition_perc = percent(Attrition_perc,accuracy = .1)
  )
colnames(Age_attrition) <- c("Age", "Total Employees","Ex Employees","Attrition %")
print(as.data.frame(Age_attrition),row.names=FALSE)

################  Attrition and Income by Age Group - Formatted for PowerPoint #############
Income_Attrition <- Frito_base %>%
  mutate(
    Income_bracket = cut(MonthlyIncome,Income_breaks,Income_labels)) %>%
      group_by(Age_Groups, Income_bracket) %>%
      summarise(
        total_employees = n(),
        Ex_employees = sum(Attrition == "Yes"),
        Attrition_perc = (Ex_employees / total_employees),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
  mutate(
    Attrition_perc = percent(Attrition_perc,accuracy = .1)
  )
colnames(Income_Attrition) <- c("Age","Monthly Income","Total Employees","Ex Employees","Attrition %")
print(as.data.frame(Income_Attrition), row.names=FALSE)

############## Attrition and Department by Age Group - Formatted for PowerPoint ############
Department_Attrition <- Frito_base %>%
  group_by(Age_Groups, Department) %>%
  summarise(
    total_employees = n(),
    Ex_employees = sum(Attrition == "Yes"),
    Attrition_perc = (Ex_employees / total_employees),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Department) %>%
  mutate(
    Attrition_perc = percent(Attrition_perc,accuracy = .1)
  )
colnames(Department_Attrition) <- c("Age","Department","Total Employees","Ex Employees","Attrition %")
print(as.data.frame(Department_Attrition), row.names=FALSE)

################ Attrition Cost by Job Level #########################
Frito_base %>%
  group_by(JobLevelName) %>%
  summarise(
    # 1. Calculate the raw numeric values first
    Attrition_Count = sum(Attrition == "Yes", na.rm = TRUE),
    Attrition_Probability = mean(Attrition == "Yes", na.rm = TRUE), # Adjust "Yes" to match your data (e.g., 1 or TRUE)
    Mean_Monthly_Attrition_Cost = mean(Attrition_Monthly_Cost, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Attrition_Cost_Ratio = mean(Attrition_Cost_Ratio, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # 2. Format the numbers for the final table display
    Attrition_Count = number(Attrition_Count),
    Attrition_Probability = percent(Attrition_Probability, accuracy = 0.1),
    Mean_Monthly_Attrition_Cost = dollar(Mean_Monthly_Attrition_Cost),
    Mean_Attrition_Cost_Ratio = percent(Mean_Attrition_Cost_Ratio)
  ) %>%
  rename(
    `Job Level` = JobLevelName,
    `Attrition Count` = Attrition_Count,
    `Attrition Probability` = Attrition_Probability,
    `Mean Monthly Attrition Cost` = Mean_Monthly_Attrition_Cost,
    `Mean Attrition Cost Ratio` = Mean_Attrition_Cost_Ratio
  ) %>%
  kable() # Removes the <chr> tags and backquotes from console view

#########################################################################################
                  ########  Unknown 300 Attrition Competition #########
#########################################################################################
CompetitionData <- read.csv(file.choose())
View(CompetitionData)

Final_nb_model <- naiveBayes(
  Attrition ~ HourlyRate + HrRate_Groups + DailyRate + MonthlyRate + MonthlyIncome + 
    Income_Groups + PercentSalaryHike + Age + Age_Groups + Gender + 
    MaritalStatus + Education + EducationField + DistanceFromHome + 
    Dist_Group + OverTime + Department + JobRole + JobLevel + 
    JobInvolvement + JobSatisfaction + EnvironmentSatisfaction + 
    RelationshipSatisfaction + PerformanceRating + WorkLifeBalance + 
    StockOptionLevel + BusinessTravel + YearsInCurrentRole + PosYears_Group + 
    YearsAtCompany + CompYears_Group + NumCompaniesWorked + 
    TrainingTimesLastYear + YearsSinceLastPromotion + TotalWorkingYears + 
    YearsWithCurrManager, 
  data = Frito_base
)
# Predict probabilities on competition dataset
pred_probs_new <- predict(Final_nb_model, newdata = CompetitionData, type = "raw")
# Apply threshold (0.4) to classify
threshold <- 0.4
yes_no_predictions <- ifelse(pred_probs_new[, "Yes"] > threshold, "Yes", "No")
# Map "Attrition"/"No Attrition" format
CompetitionData$Predicted_Attrition <- ifelse(yes_no_predictions == "Yes", "Attrition", "No Attrition")
# Export output
view(CompetitionData[, c("ID", "Predicted_Attrition")])
final_export <- CompetitionData[, c("ID","Predicted_Attrition")]
write.csv(final_export, file = "Case1PredictionsJensenAttrition.csv", row.names = FALSE)
